plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional plot of a single space curve rendered in dark blue against labeled coordinate axes. The vertical z-axis is graduated with ticks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. The x-axis runs toward the lower left with ticks labeled 2 and 4 in front and -2 and -4 behind, and the y-axis runs toward the lower right with the same labeling, 2 and 4 on the near side and -2 and -4 on the far side. The curve spirals counterclockwise around the vertical axis while climbing steadily, completing roughly two full turns between the xy-plane and the top of the frame above z = 12; its circular cross-section has radius 4, so each loop sweeps out past the ticks marked 4 on both horizontal axes. Two arrowheads placed on the ascending curve show the direction of travel. Across the upper right, in bold, the formula r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k is printed. Holding the loop radius constant while the height grows in step with the parameter is precisely what produces the spring-like shape. The plot displays the graph of a vector-valued function whose circular motion in the horizontal plane combines with uniform vertical rise to trace a helix.

elements: vertical z-axis through the origin with arrowhead at the top and label z
slanted x-axis through the origin running toward the lower left for positive x and toward the upper right for negative x, with arrowhead and label x at the positive end
slanted y-axis through the origin running toward the lower right for positive y and toward the upper left for negative y, with arrowhead and label y at the positive end
tick marks on the z-axis at z = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 with numeric labels
tick marks on the x-axis at x = -4, -2, 2, and 4 with numeric labels
tick marks on the y-axis at y = -4, -2, 2, and 4 with numeric labels
dark blue helix curve defined by r(t) = <4 cos t, 4 sin t, t> over 0 <= t <= 4π
two dark blue arrowheads tangent to the helix showing increasing t direction, one on the lower turn and one on the middle-upper turn
moving point on the helix at the current parameter value t
faded trail segment behind the moving point when animation is playing
formula label near the upper right reading r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k
live coordinate readout showing t, x(t), y(t), and z(t)
optional top-view circular projection guide in the xy-plane when top view is selected

interactions.label: Trace r(t)
interactions.teaches: The curve is generated by a point moving in a circle at constant radius while rising upward at a constant vertical rate

interactions.label: Parameter t
interactions.teaches: Each value of t maps to one position on the space curve, with x = 4 cos(t), y = 4 sin(t), and z = t changing together

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: From above, the helix becomes a radius-4 circle, showing that the horizontal motion repeats while height increases in the 3D view

interactions.label: Parametric curve
interactions.teaches: Changing the component functions changes the path, making clear that a vector-valued function draws a space curve by combining coordinate functions

demo_steps.title: Start of the curve
demo_steps.narration: At t = 0, the point begins at radius 4 in the xy-plane. The coordinates read x = 4, y = 0, z = 0.

demo_steps.title: One full revolution
demo_steps.narration: At t = 2π, the point has returned to the same horizontal position but has risen to z = 2π. The circular part repeats while the height keeps increasing.

demo_steps.title: Two full revolutions
demo_steps.narration: At t = 4π, the point has completed about two turns and reaches just above the z = 12 tick. The helix is a circle lifted steadily upward.

demo_steps.title: Look from above
demo_steps.narration: In top view, the vertical rise is hidden and the same curve collapses to a circle of radius 4 centered on the z-axis.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an axonometric/isometric-style 3D plot with no perspective convergence. World scale: x and y axes span approximately -5 to +5; z-axis spans 0 to 13.2. Positive x points diagonally down-left on screen, positive y points diagonally down-right, and positive z points straight upward. Helix formula is r(t) = <4 cos(t), 4 sin(t), t>, with t in [0, 4π] ≈ [0, 12.566]; radius is exactly 4 and vertical pitch is 2π per revolution. Draw the helix as a smooth dark blue line, color #0b4a86 or similar, tube/line width about 2 px. The lower loop begins in the xy-plane near the positive x side, winds counterclockwise as viewed from above, and rises steadily. Place tangent arrowheads on the curve around t ≈ 2.0 and t ≈ 8.0, aligned with increasing t. Axes are black or dark gray, about #111111, with small tick marks perpendicular to each axis. z tick labels appear to the right of the vertical axis at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. x-axis labels include -4 and -2 on the rear/up-right side and 2 and 4 on the front/down-left side. y-axis labels include -4 and -2 on the rear/up-left side and 2 and 4 on the front/down-right side. Formula label sits near the upper right of the plot, just to the right of the z-axis near z ≈ 12.5, reading r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k in black bold math text.
interactionPlan.notes: Sample the parametric curve with at least 300 points for a smooth helix. Equation input should parse common math functions such as sin, cos, tan, exp, sqrt, and constants pi/e; show inline parse errors and keep the last valid curve if input is invalid. The slider and animation both control the same current t value. In top view, rotate camera to look down the z-axis and optionally flatten or hide z tick labels that would clutter; keep x and y axes visible and show the circular xy projection. In 3D view, restore the original axonometric camera and vertical z-axis emphasis.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for tracing r(t): the learner plays the motion, a point moves around the circle while rising at constant speed and leaves the helix behind, making the combination of circular horizontal motion and linear vertical motion visible.
- Slider for parameter t: the learner scrubs t, the point advances along the helix with live x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), and z=t values, showing how the vector-valued function maps time to position.
- Toggle between top view and 3D view: the learner switches views, the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle from above and returns to a rising spiral in 3D, clarifying that constant radius and increasing height together form the helix.
- Equation input for the parametric curve: learner edits x(t), y(t), and z(t), pre-filled with 4*cos(t), 4*sin(t), and t; the helix redraws and the moving point follows the new curve over the same t interval.

authoredContext:
As mentioned, the name of the shape of the curve of the graph in the examplec. is a helix (the figure). The curve resembles a spring, with a circular cross-section looking down along the z-axis. It is possible for a helix to be elliptical in cross-section as well. For example, the vector-valued function r(t)=4costi+3sintj+tk describes an elliptical helix. The projection of this helix into the x,y-plane is an ellipse. Last, the arrows in the graph of this helix indicate the orientation of the curve as t progresses from 0 to 4π.

The graph of the third vector-valued function is a helix.

This figure is the graph of a helix in the 3 dimensional coordinate system. The curve represents the function r(t) = cost i + sint j + tk. The curve spirals in a circular path around the vertical z-axis and has the look of a spring. The arrows on the curve represent orientation.
